subject.title: feat(fleet): harden create, port allocation, drift visibility, and operator docs

question: Should Fleet retain an unhealthy newly created container and registry row, with its Gateway token recoverable through container inspection, as the default diagnostic behavior?
rationale: The branch deliberately trades a longer-lived secret-bearing failed artifact for operator diagnosis; code review cannot safely choose that security and recovery policy without owner intent.

options.title: Retain for diagnosis
options.body: Keep the failed cell with clear status, logs, and removal guidance plus live proof that diagnosis and cleanup work without exposing its token in normal output.

options.title: Rollback on failure
options.body: Remove the failed container and reservation to minimize retained secret-bearing artifacts, accepting reduced post-failure diagnosis.

recommendation.title: Retain for diagnosis
recommendation.body: Keep the failed cell with clear status, logs, and removal guidance plus live proof that diagnosis and cleanup work without exposing its token in normal output.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged history identifies this person as the introducer and primary recent contributor for Fleet lifecycle behavior; security CODEOWNERS should also review the audit and token-lifetime implications.
